$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for WIN-258 TRANCHE 5 -- `providers`' canonical store, the
NINTH owner behind the one PostgreSQL client ADR M0.3 §15 gives the ORM. One
entry per guard: per scope predicate, per clause the port's own contract says
must hold, per savepoint, per shape check that stands where a migration-only
CHECK stands, and per closed union a row is read back through. Each carries
the file it lives in, the EXACT text that implements it (`from`), the edit
that removes it (`to`), and the NAMED cases that were seen to go red
(`kills`).
IT IS A NINTH FILE beside mutations.json, mutations-identity.json,
mutations-ports.json, mutations-outbox.json, mutations-tools.json,
mutations-agents.json, mutations-cost.json, mutations-channels.json,
mutations-governance.json and mutations-secrets.json rather than an extension
of any of them, for the reason the others are separate: each tranche is a
separate claim about a separate port surface, and a reader checking one
should not have to read past the rest. All are hashed by the same
packages.adapters.config rule and counted together by the v1 ledger.
WHY THIS TRANCHE NEEDED ITS OWN SWEEP. `ModelPrice` is IMMUTABLE -- three
database rules refuse UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE outright with the
privileges revoked from PUBLIC on top -- so a defect written into a price
card cannot be corrected afterwards, only superseded. And the port's hardest
promises are all about what does NOT happen: a listing must apply a
JavaScript comparator the database's own collation DISAGREES with, a touch
must NOT enlist in the caller's transaction and must NOT re-date the row, a
price clash must be refused rather than converted into an update, and a
catalogue pass must NOT un-hide a model an operator hid. None of that is
visible in a returned value on a store with one caller, which is exactly the
shape of guard a green suite hides.
ONE ENTRY MAKES A GUARD STRICTER RATHER THAN LOOSER, AND IT IS DELIBERATE.
M-P43 makes `requireRateProvenance` symmetric, so an UNAVAILABLE rate
carrying a note about why it is unknown is refused by this store and accepted
by the database. `ModelPrice_rate_check` is one-directional and that is the
drift a constraints suite written only as 'the guard refuses what the CHECK
refuses' cannot see.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills and
every one was VACUOUS: a context's `dist` had been cleaned, so every suite
failed to load its import and would have 'died' against any mutation at all,
including none. The driver runs each suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to sweep
unless it is green with a non-zero executed case count, and classifies a run
with no executed cases as VACUOUS rather than as a kill. That cleaning is not
hypothetical here either: `pnpm test:v1-foundation` runs `test:clean-v1`, and
this branch watched it remove every V1 project's dist mid-run.
EACH ENTRY NAMES THE SUITE FILES IT IS SWEPT AGAINST, and the driver runs
only those. A mutation swept against the whole set would be slower and would
also hide the fact that a guard's only witness is a file nobody would think
to look in -- which is the fact the `suites` list is here to record.
THE ADAPTER'S OWN SOURCE NEEDS NO REBUILD between edits: vitest transpiles
`packages/adapters/postgres-tenancy/src/**` on the fly. The CONTEXT packages
do -- the suites resolve `@platos/context-providers` through its package
`main` and its two published subpaths, which are dist/ -- and the
`postgres-tenancy-repository` CI job builds it for exactly that reason.
RUN IT ON REAL PostgreSQL. Six of the seven suites start a container of their
own; an in-memory double cannot falsify a clause whose whole subject is what
the database does with it.
THREE SWEEPS. THE FIRST SCORED 41 KILLED, 3 SURVIVED AND 0 VACUOUS, and every
one of the three was a real finding rather than a driver artefact:
* M-P17's edit projected `SELECT 0` where the guard projects `SELECT 1`,
inside an `EXISTS` -- which treats the two identically. The edit removed
NOTHING, and a driver that could not tell a no-op edit from a surviving
guard would have scored it the same way. It is recorded here rather than
quietly repaired, and it is now the removal of the whole `OR EXISTS` block.
* M-P16's clause is written out TWICE, once per half of the pin predicate,
and the negative control seeded only the ROUTES -- so the memory
configuration's copy had no witness at all. The control now seeds both
sites, and the second copy has an entry of its own (M-P16b).
* M-P18's environment clause had no witness because the only scoped case
differed in all THREE ids, so the tenant clauses above it refused the read
before the environment clause was consulted. A project with two
environments is the ordinary shape that reaches it, and it is now a named
case.
THE SECOND SWEEP SCORED 46 KILLED, 1 SURVIVED, 0 VACUOUS, and the survivor
was the converse of the third finding above: with the environment clause
restored, the TENANT clauses had no witness, because the scoped case differed
in the environment too. The forged-ancestry case -- the right environment id
under the wrong organization and project -- now asks the pin count as well as
the four delegate reads.
THE THIRD SWEEP SCORED 47 KILLED, 0 SURVIVED, 0 VACUOUS, every one by a NAMED
case rather than by an unnamed red, and the working tree was clean afterwards.

mutations.name: M-P32 findPricesForKeys: ONE statement for any number of keys
mutations.to:
const rows: readonly JoinedPriceRow[] = (
        await Promise.all(
          [...keys].map((one) =>
            transactions.reader().$queryRaw<readonly JoinedPriceRow[]>`
              SELECT price."id", price."modelId", price."effectiveFrom",
                     price."inputRate", price."outputRate", price."cacheReadRate", price."cacheWriteRate",
                     price."inputSource", price."outputSource",
                     price."cacheReadSource", price."cacheWriteSource",
                     price."inputObservedAt", price."outputObservedAt",
                     price."cacheReadObservedAt", price."cacheWriteObservedAt",
                     price."inputSourceRef", price."outputSourceRef",
                     price."cacheReadSourceRef", price."cacheWriteSourceRef",
                     model."key" AS "modelKey",
                     model."provider" AS "modelProvider",
                     model."name" AS "modelName"
                FROM "ModelPrice" price
                JOIN "Model" model ON model."id" = price."modelId"
               WHERE price."effectiveFrom" <= ${at}
                 AND model."key" = ${one}
            `,
          ),
        )
      ).flat();
      const unusedRows = await transactions.reader().$queryRaw<readonly JoinedPriceRow[]>`
mutations.note: The join becomes ONE STATEMENT PER KEY. `model-key.ts` produces up to four candidate keys for one model string and this read is asked once per priced step, so the cost of pricing a turn grows with how many ways its model can be named.
kills: every read costs the same over a small environment and a large one > each read's statement count matches its pin, over BOTH sizes
